name: PU-12M: the regiment's order, cover the Kesmark bridges
description: Battery 21 at its position by Vrbice, seen from its PU-12M (roadmap 14.1, 14.3, G10). At 19:01 the regiment's duty officer gives the battery commander the regiment commander's order on the command net: cover the Kesmark bridges from low-flying attack, from new positions west of the bridges, ready by 20:31. The battery commander reads it back and works the textbook's sequence: the preliminary order on the battery net, the situation and his decision, the oral combat order with the emission regime and each launcher's sector, «К маршу!» to the new position on the roads, «К бою!» there across the attack direction, and «к бою готов» to the regiment. In his seat you give each of these from the crew menu's Battery orders when they are due; the order and your plan are in the map cases (O).
notes: Fictional. The task is data/campaign/tasks/bty21_cover_bridges.json, the commander's sequence data/campaign/battery_plan.json; the new positions are data/command/places_pannonia.json's bty21_bridges and bty21_bridges_reserve. The roads are the country's with the Kesmark range's tracks (simcore/nav/session.hpp).

regiment.notes: The regiment's command post and its control battery's P-19, in the Lazne woods (places_pannonia.json's rgt_cp). It designates to the battery every target within 40 km of it (sam3d) and orders readiness no. 1 at the start (code 10, data/command/aspd_codes.json).

messages.text: Regiment to the battery: readiness one; targets in the north-west sector.

radios.notes: The frequencies are SAM3D placeholders (a 1980s regiment's are not public): the command net on the R-111's preset 1, the post's own R-123M nets at least 10 % from it and not 8 or 16 MHz off (r111_to p. 3), the R-407's duplex pair 4 MHz apart and off its spurious channels (r407_plate).

radio_data.source: rrs_1986 (radio data: frequencies by conditional number, call signs; the main station of each net); flak11 (PU12-1: the five sets' nets; FuG-2 20-27 MHz and FuG-4 37-51.5 MHz on one diplexer); bstudy_tactics (the form of call signs: a word for a station, a number for an official); every value here is a sam3d placeholder
radio_data.notes: Placeholders: a 1980s regiment's radio data are not public. Each net's working frequency is its set's preset 1, its spare preset 2. They keep the R-111's rules (r111_to p. 3): the post's own sets at least 10 % from its frequency and not 8 or 16 MHz off. The battery net and the air picture are exempt from radio silence (vst_1988: air defence and the warning system).

movers.notes: The regiment's transport company bringing fuel and rations up to the battery.

nav.notes: The country's roads and the range's tracks; the chain's places as the march's and the movers' ends.

crews.notes: His set off; a field telephone line laid to the PU-12M at the position.

task.notes: The regiment commander's order, said by the regiment's duty officer on the command net in its short form; the paper follows as taken down.
